findingDetails.title: A checked completion criterion does not reproduce
findingDetails.scopeProof: ran the criterion's own command verbatim from the repository root; the single hit is in a file the criterion's two globs do not exclude
findingDetails.case: an evaluator or a later reviewer re-runs the criterion to confirm the phase is done, sees one hit where the criterion promises none, and cannot tell whether the layout rule regressed or the pattern is too broad
findingDetails.claim: The first completion criterion of phase 003 is marked done but its third command prints a hit.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: ran the other two clauses of the same criterion and both hold: 'inside the tree' appears only on the line that also names ../<name> at doctor-overlay-presentation.txt:560, and the leading-dot search prints nothing; ran the second criterion and it prints exactly one heading at overlays.md:261
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: the pattern was written before doctor-env.yaml gained the word opt-in, so the criterion was true when it was ticked and drifted afterwards; that is still a traceability defect, because a ticked criterion is read as reproducible
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: drop if the criterion is amended to exclude assets/ or to anchor the phrase to the layout rule, which makes the tick reproducible again

results.notes: six of the seven phase-003 criteria re-ran clean; the first criterion's third clause prints one hit, recorded as R7-P2-001
every documented LAYOUT form matches the code, including the mixed overflow line
D1 holds with no opt-in field, and the sibling rule D2 froze is stated with its exact refusal
each remedy names the exact command an operator runs

noveltyJustification: one new P2 (weight 1) against seven carried P2 findings (weight 7) gives a weighted new share of 0.125; the finding comes from executing the packet's own checklist rather than from reading code, which no earlier iteration did
